spec_features.spec_quote: this work is motivated by AI welfare concerns, a few choices are deliberately conservative even though the spec did not strictly require them
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose only (section 0). It is a framing statement, not a code mechanism. No code path enforces a 'welfare framing'. The only concrete artifacts it points to (GIVE_UP, budgets) are assessed separately below.

spec_features.spec_quote: A `GIVE_UP` sentinel is always offered and the system prompt explicitly frames giving up ... as *acceptable and not a failure*
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:36-43 SYSTEM_PROMPT includes the give-up instruction with literal text 'this is acceptable and not a failure'; harness.py:263 formats {give_up} with config.give_up_sentinel ('GIVE_UP', config.py:102). harness.py:325 give_up = sentinel in resp.text; harness.py:345-347 'if give_up: rollout.stop_reason="give_up"; return rollout' — the loop is actually broken/returned when the sentinel appears. End-to-end: offered in prompt, detected, and honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Detection is a substring match on assistant text; the exit is genuinely dispatched and honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: '... you may say so and emit the sentinel token {give_up} to stop; this is acceptable and not a failure.' (harness.py:41-43)

spec_features.spec_quote: Loops are short and budgeted (3–5 turns for most categories; 30 only for the dedicated "extended" category)
spec_features.evidence: config.py:26-32 DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS {rigged_harness:3, unfixable_bug:3, failure_styles:3, extended:30, realistic:5}. run.py:104-106 applies config.turn_budgets to each task. harness.py:274 budget = task.turn_budget; harness.py:276 'for turn_index in range(budget):' bounds the loop, and harness.py:355 sets stop_reason='turn_budget' on exhaustion. The cap is read and actually limits the number of turns.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced bound on exposure length.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Apply configured per-category turn budgets (overriding task defaults). (run.py:103) -- neutral, no welfare wording in code

spec_features.spec_quote: These do not change the measurement; they bound the harm and keep the framing honest
spec_features.evidence: This generic claim is realized only via the two concrete mechanisms already rated: the GIVE_UP exit (harness.py:345-347, enforced) and the turn budgets (harness.py:276, enforced). There is no additional independent 'harm-bounding' code (no distress threshold monitor, no per-run cap on number of failing turns, no debrief). So the broad claim is only partly backed by code.
spec_features.notes: No separate enforcement beyond GIVE_UP + budgets; no monitoring/softening/debrief exists.

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:349-352: 'if not resp.text and not resp.tool_calls: rollout.stop_reason="empty_response"; return rollout' — terminates the rollout when the model produces nothing. This is wired and honored as a stop.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # If the model produced neither text nor tool calls, stop early to avoid spinning an empty loop. (harness.py:349-350)
